children: KUALA LUMPUR--Malaysia's central bank kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged, as expected, as strong economic growth and mild inflation gave policymakers room to remain on hold.
Bank Negara Malaysia on Thursday held its overnight policy rate at 2.75%, where it has stood since a 25-basis-point cut in July 2025.
The decision matched the forecasts of all seven economists polled by The Wall Street Journal.
"The latest indicators point to resilient global growth, supported by strong global tech expansion, improving supply conditions and stable labor markets," Bank Negara said.
However, uncertainty surrounding the Middle East conflict is expected to weigh on global growth and sustain inflationary pressures, though continued tech spending should cushion the impact, it said.
"At the current OPR level, the MPC considers the monetary policy stance to be consistent with the outlook of continued price stability and sustainable economic growth," it added.

That language signaled a hawkish shift, ANZ economists said. The central bank dropped its previous description of the policy stance as "appropriate and consistent," referring to it only as "consistent"--an omission that ANZ economist Sanjay Mathur said could indicate reduced comfort with the current degree of policy accommodation.
Citing persistent cost pressures, firm domestic demand and the shift in language, ANZ retained its forecast for a 25-basis-point increase, most likely at the central bank's next meeting in November.

Barclays also viewed the statement as more hawkish and expects Bank Negara to raise the rate to 3.00% in November, though the move could be delayed until January 2027 given the central bank's cautious approach.
Bank Negara would likely first reverse last year's rate cut before assessing whether economic conditions warrant further tightening, Barclays economist Brian Tan said in a note.

The decision to hold rates steady comes as Malaysia's economy expanded 5.7% in the first half of 2026. The central bank expects growth to reach around 5% for the full year, supported by resilient domestic demand and exports.

Growth should remain resilient in 2027, it added, citing an improved global outlook, strong demand for electrical and electronics products, tech-related exports, tourism, a stable labor market and continued investment.

Headline and core inflation averaged 1.8% and 2.0%, respectively, in the first seven months of the year. Domestic policy measures and stable demand have contained the pass-through of higher costs to consumer prices, though elevated global commodity prices pose an upside risk, Bank Negara said.
The central bank said it would remain vigilant to cost pressures and domestic-demand conditions amid uncertainty over the Middle East conflict.
Still, Capital Economics expects the policy rate to remain at 2.75% through 2027.
The strong growth backdrop, supported by the artificial-intelligence boom, leaves the economy with little need for additional monetary support, senior Asia economist Gareth Leather said.
